places.what: A botanical garden south of Lusaka, begun in 1950 by a colonial official who named it 'My Garden' in Nyanja. It was later sold to the government.

source.publisher: Journal of the International Association of Zoo Educators, Vol. 38

places.name: Kabwata Cultural Village
places.what: A craft and arts village in Lusaka where artisans from Zambia's provinces display and sell work. It began in 1974 as a government idea to bring the country's cultures together.

places.name: Lusaka National Museum
places.what: A cultural history museum in Lusaka telling the story of Zambia in four sections. Its upper floor holds historical and cultural artefacts and its ground floor shows art from independence onward.

places.name: Soweto Market
places.what: A large trading market in western Lusaka, used by retail traders and as a wholesale point for vegetables. The claim that it is the country's largest was not confirmed in a page I could read.

facts.label: Daily activity
facts.value: Traders under tin roofs start before sunrise

source.title: What Zambia's Soweto Market Shows About Trade and Trust
source.publisher: Initiative for African Trade and Prosperity (originally The Liberalist)
source.author: Lawrence Nacidze
source.quote: Every morning before sunrise, the tin roofs of Soweto Market rattle awake with activity.
